reason: The may_preempt entry described the 30-year exemption of newly built multiple dwellings from local rent control. That is a building exemption, not a state preemption of local rules (rule 2), so may_preempt is now empty. yields_to is also cleared: the document says increases must comply with municipal ordinances as well, not that this rule stops applying where a local ordinance applies (rule 3). The local-ordinance interplay stays in requirement and coverage_text.

rule.title: No state rent control; increases must not be unconscionable
rule.requirement: New Jersey has no statewide cap on rent. A landlord cannot raise rent in the middle of a lease, must give proper written notice to end the old lease and offer a new one, and the increase cannot be unconscionable (shockingly unfair) and must follow any local rent control ordinance.
rule.requirement_es: Nueva Jersey no tiene un límite estatal sobre el alquiler. El arrendador no puede subir el alquiler a mitad del contrato, debe dar aviso por escrito para terminar el contrato anterior y ofrecer uno nuevo, y el aumento no puede ser abusivo (injusto de manera escandalosa) y debe cumplir con cualquier ordenanza local de control de alquileres.
rule.key_value: No fixed cap; increase must not be unconscionable
rule.coverage_text: Applies statewide to tenancies covered by the Anti-Eviction Act. Local rent control or rent leveling ordinances may set stricter limits; newly constructed multiple dwellings are exempt from local rent control for 30 years after completion (N.J.S.A. 2A:42-84.5), and HUD- or NJHMFA-controlled housing is not subject to municipal rent control.
rule.quote:
The increase in rent must not be 
unconscionable; it must not be so unreasonable as to shock the conscience of a fair and honest 
person and must comply with any municipal ordinances governing rent increases.
